subject: Throughput sizing: peak vs steady - follow-up and numbers
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput sizing: peak vs steady - follow-up and numbers

Alex - thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so we can line up next steps. Attaching the Workload Summary you shared and the initial notes.

Recap of requirements we heard on the call:
- Latency SLOs: p95 response time target = 300ms (hard requirement), p99 goal = 850ms; are we aligned that p95 is the must-have?
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for the client UI (most responses stream as they generate).
- Typical request shape: expect a mix of short prompts and long generative responses. Need to confirm average tokens/request.
- Concurrency/throughput: need separate steady-state vs peak numbers. You mentioned steady-state ~200 concurrent requests and peaks up to ~1200 concurrent for short bursts. Please confirm if that peak is simultaneous concurrency or short QPS spikes.

Questions we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) Average tokens per request (response tokens only and total tokens if you have them)
2) Percent of requests that require streaming vs non-streaming
3) Expected QPS during peak bursts (if you have average requests/sec during peak minute)
4) Percent of traffic that is synchronous/low-latency vs asynchronous/batch (background)

Initial capacity assumptions (ballpark):
- If avg tokens/request = 300 and peak concurrency = 1200 with streaming, tokens/sec = 300 * (responses/sec). For a conservative calc assume peak concurrency maps to ~400 responses/sec sustained during the burst window (we'll verify with your QPS).
- Steady-state: 200 concurrency, ~65 responses/sec (estimate)
- We will run a quick capacity calc and return a recommended Dedicated baseline and a burst sizing plan (autoscale tiers + fallback to smaller model variant if needed for availability).

Next steps:
- Please confirm answers to the 4 questions above (avg tokens/request, streaming %, peak QPS, async %).
- We'll produce a short capacity sketch and recommended topology (GPU count, model variant, quantization) by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed follow-up: 2026-08-07 10:00 PT for a 30-min sizing review - does that work?

Attachments: finex_workload_summary.xlsx (from your team) attached to this thread.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference - Developer-first inference for production-grade LLMs
From: Alex Johnson <alex@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@finex.com
Date: 2026-08-06T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing: peak vs steady - follow-up and numbers

Thanks Rafael - short answers below, apologies for the terse reply, looped in procurement for timeline questions.

Answers to your questions:
1) Avg tokens/request: ~350 tokens (response only). We occasionally send longer prompts but response tokens average ~350.
2) Streaming %: ~90% of user-facing requests must stream token-by-token. The background jobs are non-streaming but small volume.
3) Peak QPS: during the hourly bursts we see ~420 responses/sec for ~60-90 seconds (these are short-lived but they hit concurrency). Those bursts happen roughly every hour during business hours.
4) Async/batch: ~15% of total volume - mostly offline scoring.

Confirming concurrency mapping: the 1200 number I gave earlier is a peak concurrent sessions number; for sizing purposes use the observed peak QPS above (420 RPS sustained for ~1-2 minutes). Steady-state is ~200 concurrency / ~65 RPS.

We need to understand cost tradeoffs and whether you can guarantee p95 < 400ms at peak. If Redwood recommends a Dedicated baseline + burst pool, can you give a rough cost range before we go to procurement?

Yes to the 10:00 PT slot on 2026-08-07 - I'll send a calendar invite.

Alex
VP Product, Finex
alex@finex.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@finex.com
Date: 2026-08-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing: peak vs steady - follow-up and numbers

Alex - perfect, this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications and immediate next actions: 

Clarifications:
- Treat the 420 RPS sustained for 60-90s as the primary peak signal; we'll size for that burst with headroom.
- We'll assume 90% streaming and avg 350 tokens/response for capacity checks.

What I'll deliver before the 10:00 PT call tomorrow:
1) A one-page capacity sketch (attached: redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.pdf) showing tokens/sec, estimated GPU count for your preferred model class, and an autoscale plan (baseline Dedicated + burst pool using lower-cost shared capacity).
2) Rough cost bands (monthly committed baseline + estimated incremental burst spend per peak-minute). These will be +/- 20% until we validate traffic shapes.
3) A short checklist for procurement (SLA options, data residency, SOC2 artifacts link).

Immediate asks for you (quick):
- If you can drop a sample traffic CSV (timestamp, request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out) into the Drive folder linked below, we can run a quick script to produce a tighter capacity estimate before the call. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finex-workload
- Confirm whether you have any hard constraints on model variant (open Llama, gpt-3.5-equivalent, etc.) or if you want Redwood recommendations.

We will aim to show a baseline that meets p95 <= 300ms on your preferred model family; if your requirement relaxes to p95 <= 400ms we can trade down model size or add more efficient batching to reduce cost. We'll call out the tradeoffs clearly.

Thanks - see you on the call 2026-08-07 10:00 PT.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_capacity_estimate_v1.pdf
